articles.title: My favorite family heirloom: an old Zojirushi hot water dispenser better than any tea kettle
articles.summary: It heats water up fast and crucially, keeps it warm for the whole day, so you can can access hot water to your heart’s content. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: O f all the things my mother has given me from the vast warehouse of her garage, there are two items I treasure the most. One, a Costco-sized box of gallon-sized Ziploc bags, and two, a battered Zojirushi water boiler that has been in the family for decades. The Ziploc bags are nice to have and can be easily replaced; the water boiler, on the other hand, has become an indispensable tool that makes my life at home a little better, every time I use it.

A brief twist: if given the choice, I’d take an ice cold beverage over hot any time. But even I, with my preference for drinks so cold that they hurt my teeth, have been converted to my family’s beloved Zojirushi.

I use it almost every day – for the instant Cafe Bustelo coffee that I drink every morning, for instant noodles, for tea and hot chocolate and any other wintry weather beverage. Once you’ve opened your heart (and wallet) to one of these things, I promise you that you will never look back.

articles.title: Grindr pays £26m to settle UK lawsuit over allegedly sharing users’ HIV status
articles.summary: US-owned dating app allegedly allowed ad firms access to private information in breach of UK law. Business live – latest updates. Grindr will pay £26m to settle a lawsuit brought by thousands of users in the UK who allege that the US dating app shared highly sensitive personal information…
body: The settlement brings to an end a two-year legal battle, after the UK law firm Austen Hays filed a claim at the high court of England and Wales in April 2024 on behalf of Grindr users alleging violations of UK privacy laws during a period up to early 2020.
The London law firm represented 12,000 people, who will receive an average compensation of £2,167 each, if the £26m is equally distributed.

Grindr was founded in 2009 to make it easier to coordinate hookups for gay men. It now claims to be the world’s largest dating app for gay, bi, trans and queer people, with nearly 15 million users around the world.

Grindr said in a US regulatory filing that it had resolved the UK group action related to what it described as “historical data practices before 2020”, when Grindr was owned and controlled by the Chinese gaming company Beijing Kunlun Tech.

articles.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Harold, the halls of residence cat, who looked after me when I first left home
articles.summary: He was the gorgeous furry tabby who made my day, even when he waltzed into my flat just to finish my takeaway. Now he’s a campus celeb, with a part-time job guarding the doors of the village shop.
body: I n 2022, when I moved into halls of residence at the University of Sheffield, my biggest concern was no longer having a furry friend to come home to, as I’d had a cat since I was 11 years old. Then I met Harold.

My first encounter with this gorgeous tabby was quite unusual. One day, in our 10-bed flat, a flurry of messages appeared on the group WhatsApp chat after my fellow roommates caught an intruder on the sofa, innocently munching on my leftover pizza.

As in many homes for first year university students, there were plenty of unfinished takeaways lying around the kitchen. And Harold was a smart cat with a clear goal: food. Any time he saw a snack or sensed one from a distance, he would come running. A can of tuna. A block of cheese. The occasional pancake. And I was more than happy to feed him – he probably had a better diet than me.
points: He was the gorgeous furry tabby who made my day, even when he waltzed into my flat just to finish my takeaway.
Now he’s a campus celeb, with a part-time job guarding the doors of the village shop.

articles.title: Why are so many people stealing from restaurants?
articles.summary: About a quarter of British adults admit to having pilfered something from a pub or restaurant. Is it an Insta-fuelled craze, or just old-fashioned greed? Knives, candles, a toilet roll holder complete with screws and Rawlplugs – that’s just some of the stuff Michelin-starred restaurants in France…
body: A Québécois restaurateur complained about similar thefts in July – a picnic table, a painting and even the thermostat had been pinched – and British restaurateurs confirm it happens in the UK, too. Jan Ostle of Wilsons in Bristol told the BBC’s World at One that the mother-of-pearl spoons he uses to serve herb sorbet are a particular target: “Every few months I have to buy another 28.”

It’s an age-old, frequently aired story – all down to a sense of entitlement, or the desire for a souvenir, or booze-fuelled bravado – but it seems awfully retro. Wasn’t trousering a Conran restaurant ashtray a quintessential 90s petty crime? We’re supposed to be into “ experiences, not things ” now, and isn’t the whole point of posting a boring Instagram carousel of seven badly lit amuse -bouches to show everyone you’ve been somewhere fancy without stealing a side plate?

articles.title: Why Can’t You Wear White After Labor Day?
articles.summary: Here’s where this archaic rule came from—and why it no longer necessarily holds true.
body: It is a truth universally acknowledged that you can’t wear white after Labor Day. But why? It’s a fashion rule that has been parroted by grandmothers, general interest magazines, and teenage mean girls for generations, as if it’s a statute that society has always abided by. Break it and— the horror! —you’re committing a sartorial sin.

As with so many American fashion edicts, though, its origins can be traced back to the elite of the Gilded Age. Every summer, they would decamp from the crowded, sweltering city to cooler places by the ocean, such as Newport or Southampton, for the entire season. Packed in their trunks were wardrobes of white.

It was a practical choice, above all: back then, it was wholly inappropriate to wear tank tops, shorts, or mini-dresses even as the temperatures soared. White, which reflects light, keeps the wearer cooler. Plus, linen —a popular, breathable fabric especially for suits back then—usually came in neutral tones.

articles.title: Inside Parker Posey’s Venice Film Festival—From Sightseeing to Fabulous Fashions
articles.summary: The star touched down in Venice for her film “Wild Horse Nine” this week. “I like looking like I’m showing up,” says Parker Posey.
body: Every year, the Venice Film Festival produces some of the most glitzy and glamorous red carpets outside of Hollywood—but Parker Posey is one of the few stars you can guarantee is having the most fun doing it all.

The actor took her own turn on the Lido to premiere her new film, Martin McDonagh’s Wild Horse Nine, which is one of the buzziest projects on the 2026 roster. (She co-stars alongside John Malkovich, Sam Rockwell, and Steve Buscemi.) “Venice is a magical city, and getting to celebrate Wild Horse Nine here is a treat,” says Posey of her whirlwind week at the enduringly chic festival. “I can’t not think of the Renaissance when I’m in Italy—the power of art and the presence of religion—all surrounded by water and reflections. Its baroque beauty is lush and bold!”

Before Posey began to think about attending the photo call and premiere—and, of course, dressing the part—she made sure to take some time for herself. After all, one must sightsee in the romantic, canaled Italian city. “I walked around at every break I’ve had over these past four days,” she says. “I’d find myself in churches lighting candles for my mom, who had surgery this week.”

articles.title: 28 Travel Jackets for Every Climate, Itinerary, and Jet-Setting Style
articles.summary: Before you hit the road this fall, be sure to pack the right travel jacket for your itinerary—from lightweight cotton styles to designer raincoats, here are some of our favorites.
body: Everyone has a favorite jacket (or two) in their daily rotation, but what constitutes a go-to piece for everyday life doesn’t always translate to the road. After all, the ideal travel jacket should be pulling double duty on your journey; it should be practical for your in-transit moments, but endlessly versatile for any activity you have planned once you arrive.

The first order of business is portability. You’ll likely want something lightweight that can fold easily into a suitcase when it’s not needed. Cotton, nylon, and linen will be your friends in that case—easy to pack away and easy to layer over sweaters or tees when the weather calls for it. Luckily, these materials come in almost every style, from sporty nylon front-zips to cotton utility jackets. If you need something a little more heavy-duty, look no further than a leather or denim option. And if you don’t already have a trench or raincoat in your wardrobe, now is the time to invest. You never know when an unexpected shower could disrupt a day of sightseeing.

articles.title: How to Style a Suede Jacket—6 Fall-Ready Outfits to Try
articles.summary: Textural, cool, and endlessly versatile, suede jackets are a fall—and Fashion Month!—favorite for a reason. Here are six ways how to style a suede jacket now.
body: We love suede almost all year round, but the supple material shines the most in fall. Suede boots, bags, and ballet flats top our seasonal shopping lists, but the suede jacket is king. Softer and more supple than your typical leather bomber, but with the same off-duty attitude, a suede jacket is as essential as it gets.

Those looking for an everyday style have plenty to choose from this season—each with their own particular personality, from Prada’s feminine cut with a curved collar to Nour Hammour’s slouchy bomber style. The shirt jacket (or “shacket”, as it’s fondly known) makes an appearance in suede, too: Banana Republic’s reissued utility style looks great with baggy denim, while a Toteme button-down style adds edge to a floral skirt. And luckily, there are options across the price spectrum. Brands like J.Crew and Coach offer chic styles that hold their own against high-end designer takes.
Take a cue from Vogue’s head of editorial content, Chloe Malle, and style a cropped suede topper with a cheery red knit and floral trousers.
Toteme’s suede “shacket” and Miu Miu’s Mary Jane loafers tone down the sharp femininity of a floral pencil skirt.

I’m always quick to dismiss anything that’s complicated to clean, and they often uncover durability issues within a matter of days. Our combined criteria have left us with a pretty short short-list of reusable water bottles that are durable, dishwasher-safe, spill-proof, and (save for the sippy-style Nalgene I recommend for toddlers) almost completely leakproof when properly closed.

articles.title: The World’s Most Beautiful Libraries Worth Traveling For
articles.summary: From converted monasteries to redwood forested reading rooms, the most beautiful libraries are for truly ones for the books.
body: The most beautiful libraries have long been more than places to check out books, though some make a particularly compelling case for lingering. As a demand for third places to gather outside of home or work continues to grow, libraries are having a moment as prime spots for idling, browsing, and simply taking a break from the bustle beyond of their opulent doors.

Libraries have taken on an array of forms around the world, as reading rooms that have been tucked into former monasteries, designed as futuristic cultural hubs, and constructed in the heart of the California redwoods. While the books are still the main attraction, it certainly doesn’t hurt to be surrounded by ornate frescoes or unexpected nooks that make you want to stay a while longer. From Colombia to Qatar, these 11 libraries are worth building into your next trip, whether you are architecture-obsessed or longing to sit down in a picturesque setting with a new read.
